findings.title: Early return when `dateOverrideExist` is true skips all busy-time and booking checks
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a slot falls within a date override on that day, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately execute `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before reaching `return busy.every(...)` at line 153. As a result, whenever a host has a date override on a day, all existing Cal.com bookings, external calendar busy periods, and event buffers for that day are completely ignored, allowing double-bookings during any date override. The `workingHours` check at line 138 should instead be guarded by `if (!dateOverrideExist)` so execution continues to the `busy.every(...)` check.

findings.title: Broken date override boundary, equality, day-matching, and multi-range checks in `checkIfIsAvailable`
findings.body:
The `dateOverrides.find` block in `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 105-131) has several logic errors:
1. Line 114 compares two newly constructed `Dayjs` instances with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which compares object references and is always `false`, so full-day unavailable overrides where `start` equals `end` are never detected by this check.
2. Lines 117-125 only reject a slot if `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`, instead of rejecting when `slotStartTime < overrideStart` or `slotEndTime > overrideEnd`. Slots that partially overlap the start or end of the override (or start exactly at `overrideEnd`) are erroneously allowed.
3. Using `dateOverrides.find` to return `false` when a slot falls outside any single override on that day breaks multiple override windows on the same day (e.g., 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00), since a slot in the first window is rejected by the second window and vice versa.
4. Lines 109-111 compare `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` using the shifted UTC date (and local server timezone on `dayjs(date.start)`), rather than comparing the slot's date in `organizerTimeZone` against the override's calendar date (`dayjs.utc(date.start).format("YYYY MM DD")`). When a slot or override crosses midnight UTC, the dates do not match and the override is either ignored on the actual day or applied to the wrong UTC day.

findings.title: `workingHours` check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end`, allows non-working days, and breaks split shifts
findings.body:
Lines 138-151 check whether a slot falls within `workingHours`, but contain three bugs:
1. Line 142 computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` using `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so a slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end extends past `workingHour.endTime` is not rejected.
2. If a host has no working hours on `slotStartTime.day()` (e.g., a fixed host does not work on Saturdays while a round-robin host does), `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` is `false` for every entry, so `workingHours.find(...)` returns `undefined` and `checkIfIsAvailable` treats the host as available all day on their day off.
3. If a host has multiple `workingHours` entries for the same day (either from a split schedule like 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, or because their working hours cross midnight UTC and `getWorkingHours` splits them into two entries on the same day), `workingHours.find(...)` returns `true` because any slot will be outside at least one of the entries, rejecting all slots for that host.

findings.title: Timezone offset shift on date overrides wraps around midnight and double-applies DST
findings.body:
In `getSlots` (lines 206-225), converting date overrides to invitee local minutes fails when the timezone difference crosses midnight or a DST boundary:
1. Lines 218-223 compute `startTime` and `endTime` using `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` after `.add(offset, "minute")`. Because `.hour()` wraps modulo 24, if adding `offset` pushes `end` to or past midnight in the invitee's timezone (e.g., 24:00 becomes `0`, or 02:00 next day becomes `120`), `endTime` becomes less than or equal to `startTime`, causing `buildSlots` (`if (start >= end) continue`) to drop the override slots completely.
2. Line 207 filters `activeOverrides` by checking if `dayjs.utc(override.start)` (which stores the organizer's wall-clock time as UTC) is between `startOfInviteeDay` and `startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day")` without subtracting `organizerUtcOffset` first. When the override falls on a different calendar date in the invitee's timezone than in the organizer's timezone, `activeOverrides` matches it on the wrong invitee day (shifted by 24 hours) or misses it.
3. Lines 212-214 compute `offset` using the UTC offsets at `override.start`, but `buildSlots` (lines 102-110) subsequently adds `organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff` (the DST offset difference between `dayjs()` today and `startOfInviteeDay`) to every slot, shifting date override slots by an extra hour when booked across a DST transition.

findings.title: Missing tests for round-robin fixed-host date overrides and date overrides with existing bookings
findings.body: The PR only adds an assertion for a single-user event with a +30 minute timezone difference (`Asia/Kolkata` to `Asia/Dhaka`). There are no tests for a round-robin event where a fixed host has a date override (one of the primary bugs this PR targets) and no tests for a date override on a day that also has an existing booking or calendar busy time.
